sources_considered.why: Primary disclosure of quarterly expenditure, its cloud and AI allocation, spending intentions and AI-related growth.
Contemporaneous customer-side survey evidence, retained as context because it covers AI broadly and does not measure Microsoft customers' generative AI profits.

evidence_items.locator: Amy Hood prepared remarks, paragraph beginning Capital expenditures
evidence_items.explanation: Supports the rounded expenditure figure; the adjacent passage assigns nearly all of it to cloud and AI together. The same disclosure reports AI-related sales growth and plans for higher spending, but neither establishes AI profit or customer financial returns.

metric_scope.metric: Capital expenditure including finance leases, predominantly cloud and AI

evidence_items.explanation: The survey reports perceived gains in efficiency, productivity and customer satisfaction among AI-investing organizations. This cautions against assuming users received no benefit, but its population and measures do not settle Microsoft's generative AI customer returns.

unresolved_gaps: No comparable disclosure isolates Microsoft's generative AI revenue, attributable costs and profit for the target quarter.
No representative measurement establishes financial returns for Microsoft's generative AI customers in that quarter.
The claim supplies no threshold for not much money.
The reviewed record does not establish the historical superlative about spending more than ever before on a technology.
